phenomena.label: Past participle agreement with subject
phenomena.hypothesis: Past participles agree in gender and number with the subject when the auxiliary is être, but not with avoir.
phenomena.note: être triggers subject agreement (Elle est arrivée); avoir does not agree with the subject (Elle a mangé, not *mangée).

phenomena.label: Binding (Principles A, B, C)
phenomena.hypothesis: Reflexives must be locally bound (A), pronouns must be locally free (B), and R-expressions must be free (C).
phenomena.note: Principle A requires local reflexive se for coreference; Principle B forbids reflexive across a clause boundary for intended cross-clause coreference; Principle C concerns R-expression distribution (C'est Léon vs *Il est Léon).

phenomena.label: Control vs Raising
phenomena.hypothesis: Subject control identifies the understood subject of the infinitive, which is diagnosable via adjective agreement.
phenomena.note: In subject-control 'Marie a promis à Paul de rester seule', the infinitival subject is Marie (feminine), so the adjective must be feminine (seule), not masculine (*seul).

phenomena.label: Past participle agreement with preposed object (COD vs COI)
phenomena.hypothesis: With avoir, the past participle agrees with a preposed direct object (COD) but not with an indirect object (COI).
phenomena.note: COD triggers agreement (La pomme que Max a mangée); COI does not (L'amie à qui Max a téléphoné, not *téléphonée).

phenomena.label: Subjunctive mood selection
phenomena.hypothesis: The subjunctive is licensed only in contexts that require it (e.g. il faut que) and is barred where the indicative is required (e.g. espérer que).
phenomena.note: il faut que requires subjunctive (pleuve); espérer que requires indicative (vient). Some forms are homophonous between subjunctive and indicative for je/tu/il, distinct only for nous/vous.

phenomena.label: Adjective position (prenominal vs postnominal)
phenomena.hypothesis: French adjectives occupy a fixed prenominal or postnominal position depending on the adjective class.
phenomena.note: Numerals and certain short adjectives (belle, vieux, vieil) are prenominal; most descriptive adjectives (verte, française) are postnominal. Some adjectives change meaning by position (une seule femme 'only' vs une femme seule 'alone'; ma propre maison 'own' vs ma maison propre 'clean') and may need longer context.

phenomena.label: Subject extraction (que vs qui)
phenomena.hypothesis: Extraction of an embedded subject requires the complementizer qui rather than que (the que-to-qui rule).
phenomena.note: Subject extraction across an embedded clause selects qui, not que.

templates.name: Subject agreement with être auxiliary
templates.note: être requires the participle to agree with the feminine subject.

templates.name: No subject agreement with avoir auxiliary
templates.note: avoir does not trigger agreement with the subject.

templates.name: Principle A (local reflexive)
templates.note: Under the coreferent reading, a local reflexive se is required; the pronoun le cannot corefer with Léon.

templates.name: Principle B (cross-clause coreference)
templates.grammatical: Léon pense que Gertrude le voit.
templates.ungrammatical: Léon pense que Gertrude se voit.
templates.translation: Léon thinks that Gertrude sees him.
templates.note: For intended cross-clause coreference with Léon, the pronoun le is required; the reflexive se would be bound locally by Gertrude.

templates.name: Principle C (R-expression)
templates.note: Identifying an R-expression requires the C'est construction, not Il est.

templates.name: Subject control and adjective agreement
templates.grammatical: Marie a promis à Paul de rester seule.
templates.ungrammatical: Marie a promis à Paul de rester seul.
templates.translation: Marie promised Paul to remain alone.
templates.note: Subject control identifies the infinitival subject as Marie; the adjective agreement (feminine seule) diagnoses it.

templates.name: Agreement with preposed direct object (COD)
templates.grammatical: La pomme que Max a mangée
templates.ungrammatical: La pomme que Max a mangé
templates.note: The preposed direct object triggers past participle agreement with avoir.

templates.name: No agreement with indirect object (COI)
templates.grammatical: L'amie à qui Max a téléphoné
templates.ungrammatical: L'amie à qui Max a téléphonée
templates.note: An indirect object (COI) does not trigger past participle agreement.

templates.name: Subjunctive required (il faut que)
templates.note: il faut que requires the subjunctive; the indicative pleut is ungrammatical.

templates.name: Subjunctive barred (espérer que)
templates.translation: I hope that he is coming today
templates.note: espérer que takes the indicative, not the subjunctive. Forms are homophonous in subjunctive/indicative except for nous/vous.

templates.name: Prenominal vs postnominal adjective placement
templates.note: belle is prenominal. Some adjectives change meaning by position (seul, propre) and may require longer context.

templates.name: que vs qui in subject extraction
templates.grammatical: J'employais les expressions que je savais qui le choqueraient le moins
templates.ungrammatical: J'employais les expressions que je savais que le choqueraient le moins
templates.translation: I used the expressions that I knew would shock him the least
templates.note: Subject extraction requires the complementizer qui, not que.
